observations: A large rounded head shape sits against a flat magenta background, outlined in thick black lines, with yellow angular forms rising from the top edge.
Two asymmetric eye zones dominate the upper face: the left is a crossed square filled with red hatching, the right a circular form with radiating red lines around a blue oval center.
The open mouth shows a row of white teeth rendered as dense parallel strokes, while loose white and red scribble lines scatter across the blue and purple mid-face.
reading: The face pushes forward on its flat magenta field, thick black outlines holding together a surface that keeps splitting into competing zones. The two eye forms refuse to match — one gridded and crossed, one radial and open. Bared teeth read as confrontational, yet loose scribble lines across the cheeks pull that edge toward something closer to unease.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between title neighbors #90 and #92. Where #90 uses a black ground and blended flesh tones for quieter tension, #91 returns to a saturated magenta field also visible in nnotb #187, linking the two owned collections through shared background color and yellow line work.

connections.reason: Both works show a rounded head with exposed teeth, but #90 uses a black ground and blended flesh tones against #91's flat magenta and hard outlines, making the tonal contrast between the two direct and visible.
nnotb #187 shares the same saturated magenta background and yellow line forms with #91, and both pack the picture surface with layered marks that leave little open space.

lookingQuestion: The two eye zones use completely different internal structures — one crossed and gridded, one radial and open — so what does that asymmetry do to how you read the face as a whole?
ambiguities: Small red marks near the upper corners are partially obscured by overlapping lines; their role in the composition is unclear.
The spiral form at the right edge of the face could be read as an ear or as a separate decorative element; the image does not resolve this.
